name: The 10% brain myth, debunked
description: Everyone believes you only use 10% of your brain. That's a myth with a 90-year-old motivational origin and zero scientific basis. The evidence: brain scans show all regions active, and your brain burns 20% of your energy for just 2% of your weight.

facts.claim: The ten-percent-of-the-brain myth states humans use only a small fraction of their brain; it has no scientific basis

The myth likely originated from the 'reserve energy' theories of William James in the 1890s and was popularized in the 1920s-1930s self-help era, including the 1929 World Almanac and a 1936 foreword to Dale Carnegie's book
Brain imaging (PET, fMRI) shows all parts of the brain are active almost all the time, including during sleep
The brain uses up to 20% of the body's energy while making up only about 2% of body weight
There is almost no brain area that can be damaged without loss of abilities
The myth has been misattributed to Albert Einstein, with no documented quote
